Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the estimate lists a clean and adjust of the shutter assembly at one hundred eighty dollars a replacement advance pawl at sixty five dollars and labor for removing the top plate and checking the meter at ninety dollars the inspection fee of thirty dollars is already included in that labor line the estimate does not include a meter replacement a curtain replacement or shipping if those become necessary we need to call jonah and ask before adding any of those charges he asked whether the shop could keep the total below four hundred dollars and i told him the current estimate is below that amount but additional parts could change it

number one the shutter check includes photographing both curtains under the bench lamp and recording the travel time at one sixtieth one thirtieth and one fifteenth number two the advance pawl should be compared with the sample part in drawer c twelve before ordering because two versions look almost alike number three the meter test needs to be repeated after the top plate is back on and the battery contact is cleaned number four the dent should be left alone unless jonah approves cosmetic work the bench notes say not to press the rewind knob or try to straighten the top plate while the camera is assembled

i need to forward the estimate and the intake photographs to jonah and lena this afternoon the photographs show the dent the advance lever and the pale band on the test frame i will attach the bench note as a separate file and label it nq four one seven initial inspection i have not included the brass key in the photographs because it is still in the small envelope with the strap the key is marked boathouse and jonah said it is not a camera case key so it should stay with his belongings at the counter

if the shutter test stays within the service range after cleaning and the sample pawl matches the part in drawer c twelve then the current estimate should cover the work if either condition fails we need jonah's approval before ordering another part or changing the estimate if the meter still reads low after the contact is cleaned we should report the reading but not assume the meter needs replacement the camera should remain on the blue shelf until jonah replies the shelf tag has his name and nq four one seven and the repair status is marked estimate pending

jonah also mentioned that the harbor archive has a small exhibit opening on the eighteenth of october but he said the camera is not required for the opening and he does not want us to rush the work he would prefer to collect it in person because the strap and key belong together the counter schedule shows that he is available on tuesday or thursday after four if he decides to proceed he asked whether we could keep the original estimate and any later approval in one folder so that lena can see what was agreed

the estimate is dated september ninth and lists a projected bench time of three to five business days after approval that is a time range and not a promised pickup date the parts book shows the advance pawl is normally in stock but drawer c twelve still needs to be checked before we can rely on that note the receipt copy is clipped behind the estimate and the intake ticket remains in the envelope with the key the last note on the paper says call before any change above the current estimate and keep the camera on the blue shelf while waiting for jonah's answer", "output": "This is Mara Ellis dictating notes for the estimate on the Leica M6 that came into North Quay Camera on Monday. The body belongs to Jonah Price, and it arrived in a canvas shoulder bag with a brass key tied to the strap. Jonah said the camera was his father's and that he uses it for neighborhood portraits and the harbor archive. He asked for a written estimate before anyone starts work, and he wants the old parts returned if the repair goes ahead. The intake ticket is NQ 417. The serial number ends in 826, and the silver body has a dent beside the rewind knob.

At the counter, I tested the meter with a fresh battery, and the needle moved slowly before stopping just below the mark for one-sixtieth. The shutter curtains travel, but the first curtain hesitates at the lower edge and leaves a narrow pale band on the test frame. The film advance lever moves with a rough click on the second stroke, and the frame counter stops between three and four. The viewfinder has dust near the right side, but the glass is not cracked. Jonah said the pale band has appeared on only two rolls, and he has not noticed it on every frame.

The estimate lists a clean and adjust of the shutter assembly at one hundred eighty dollars, a replacement advance pawl at sixty-five dollars, and labor for removing the top plate and checking the meter at ninety dollars. The inspection fee of thirty dollars is already included in that labor line. The estimate does not include a meter replacement, a curtain replacement, or shipping. If those become necessary, we need to call Jonah and ask before adding any of those charges. He asked whether the shop could keep the total below four hundred dollars, and I told him the current estimate is below that amount, but additional parts could change it.

Number one: The shutter check includes photographing both curtains under the bench lamp and recording the travel time at one-sixtieth, one-thirtieth, and one-fifteenth.

Number two: The advance pawl should be compared with the sample part in drawer C12 before ordering, because two versions look almost alike.

Number three: The meter test needs to be repeated after the top plate is back on and the battery contact is cleaned.

Number four: The dent should be left alone unless Jonah approves cosmetic work. The bench notes say not to press the rewind knob or try to straighten the top plate while the camera is assembled.

When I called Jonah, he said, “Please send the estimate to me and copy my sister, Lena Price, because she is helping with the archive expenses.” He gave the address as jonah.price@shoremail.net and said Lena uses lena.price@postbox.org. He asked that we use email rather than leave a message at his office, and said he usually checks mail after six. His exact words were, “I want to see the parts listed separately, and I do not want the camera opened any farther until I answer.” I read back the two email addresses, and he confirmed both of them.

I need to forward the estimate and the intake photographs to Jonah and Lena this afternoon. The photographs show the dent, the advance lever, and the pale band on the test frame. I will attach the bench note as a separate file and label it “NQ 417 initial inspection.” I have not included the brass key in the photographs because it is still in the small envelope with the strap. The key is marked “boathouse,” and Jonah said it is not a camera case key, so it should stay with his belongings at the counter.

If the shutter test stays within the service range after cleaning and the sample pawl matches the part in drawer C12, then the current estimate should cover the work. If either condition fails, we need Jonah's approval before ordering another part or changing the estimate. If the meter still reads low after the contact is cleaned, we should report the reading but not assume the meter needs replacement. The camera should remain on the blue shelf until Jonah replies. The shelf tag has his name and NQ 417, and the repair status is marked “estimate pending.”

Jonah also mentioned that the harbor archive has a small exhibit opening on the eighteenth of October, but he said the camera is not required for the opening and he does not want us to rush the work. He would prefer to collect it in person because the strap and key belong together. The counter schedule shows that he is available on Tuesday or Thursday after four. If he decides to proceed, he asked whether we could keep the original estimate and any later approval in one folder so that Lena can see what was agreed.

The estimate is dated September ninth and lists a projected bench time of three to five business days after approval. That is a time range and not a promised pickup date. The parts book shows the advance pawl is normally in stock, but drawer C12 still needs to be checked before we can rely on that note. The receipt copy is clipped behind the estimate, and the intake ticket remains in the envelope with the key. The last note on the paper says, “Call before any change above the current estimate, and keep the camera on the blue shelf while waiting for Jonah's answer.”"}]
